title: Colonial-Era Heritage in India: Portuguese, French, Danish and British Towns
seoTitle: Colonial-Era Heritage in India: Where to See It | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: India's colonial-era heritage, seen honestly: Old Goa, Kochi, Puducherry, Tranquebar, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Shimla, New Delhi and the Cellular Jail.
description: A guide to colonial-era heritage in India, seen in its full context: Portuguese Old Goa, Diu and Daman; Dutch and Portuguese Kochi; Danish Tharangambadi and Serampore; French Puducherry and Chandannagar; and British-era Chennai, Kolkata, Mumbai, Shimla and New Delhi, along with memorials to the freedom struggle such as the Cellular Jail and Jallianwala Bagh.
dek: European powers left churches, forts, offices and whole towns across India. They are worth seeing, and worth seeing with the history they carry.

hero.alt: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai

intro: From the 16th century, Portuguese, Dutch, Danish, French and British trading companies set up forts and settlements on India's coasts. The British East India Company, and after 1858 the British Crown, went on to rule most of the subcontinent until 1947. That rule was imposed and kept by force, and it drained wealth, reshaped economies and was marked by famines and violence, as well as by the long struggle that ended it.

The buildings of that period are now part of India's heritage, used as courts, stations, museums, churches and homes, and several are UNESCO sites. This guide covers where to see them, and the memorials that tell the other side of the story.
quickAnswer: India's main colonial-era heritage is found in Portuguese Old Goa (UNESCO), Diu and Daman; Fort Kochi and Mattancherry in Kerala; French Puducherry; Danish Tharangambadi; and British-era Kolkata, Mumbai (CSMT and the Victorian and Art Deco ensembles, both UNESCO), Chennai's Fort St George, Shimla and New Delhi. Memorials such as the Cellular Jail in Port Blair and Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar remember the freedom struggle.
takeaways: Old Goa's churches and Mumbai's CSMT and Victorian and Art Deco ensembles are UNESCO sites.
Kochi shows Portuguese, Dutch and British layers alongside Jewish and Kerala heritage.
Puducherry's French Quarter is the best-preserved French town plan in India.
Kolkata and Mumbai have the richest British-era architecture.
Visit the Cellular Jail or Jallianwala Bagh to see the cost of colonial rule.

Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Shimla, New Delhi

items.name: Old Goa
body: The Basilica of Bom Jesus, Se Cathedral and other 16th- and 17th-century churches of a once-great Portuguese city. The Inquisition in Goa is part of this history too.

image.alt: The Basilica of Bom Jesus, Old Goa
image.caption: Basilica of Bom Jesus

items.name: Kochi
body: St Francis Church, the Chinese fishing nets, the Mattancherry Palace (built by the Portuguese for the Raja of Kochi and later renovated by the Dutch) and the Paradesi Synagogue.

items.name: Diu and Daman
body: Portuguese forts and churches, under Portuguese rule until 1961.

items.name: Puducherry
body: The French Quarter's grid of streets, yellow villas and churches by the sea; French rule ended in 1954.

items.name: Tharangambadi and Serampore
body: Fort Dansborg (1620) in Tamil Nadu, and the Danish town of Serampore near Kolkata, where Serampore College was founded in 1818.

items.name: Kolkata
body: Capital of British India until 1911: the Victoria Memorial, Writers' Building, St Paul's Cathedral and the old Dalhousie Square.

items.name: Mumbai
body: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (UNESCO 2004) and the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles (UNESCO 2018) around the Oval Maidan and Marine Drive.

image.alt: The Gateway of India, Mumbai, built in the Indo-Saracenic style
image.caption: Gateway of India, Mumbai

items.name: Chennai
body: Fort St George (begun in 1644) with St Mary's Church, and the Indo-Saracenic High Court.

items.name: Shimla and New Delhi
body: Shimla, the summer capital, with the former Viceregal Lodge; New Delhi, designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker and inaugurated in 1931.

sections.heading: Memorials of the freedom struggle
list: The Cellular Jail in Port Blair, where political prisoners were held in solitary cells; now a national memorial.
Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, where British troops fired on an unarmed crowd in 1919.
Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad, from where Gandhi began the Salt March in 1930.
The Red Fort, where the INA trials were held in 1945 and 1946.

sections.heading: Architectural styles
paras: Colonial-era buildings in India cover several styles. Portuguese Baroque shaped the churches of Goa. The British built in neoclassical style in early Kolkata and Chennai, then in Victorian Gothic in 19th-century Mumbai. Indo-Saracenic architecture, which borrowed domes, arches and chhatris from Indian traditions, appears in Chennai's High Court and Mumbai's Gateway of India. Art Deco followed in the 1930s along Mumbai's Marine Drive. Much of this work was designed by Indian engineers and built by Indian craftsmen, and Indian architects also shaped these styles.

sections.heading: Walks to take
list: Mumbai's Fort precinct: CSMT, the Bombay High Court, the University and the Oval Maidan.
Kolkata's BBD Bagh (Dalhousie Square) and the Park Street cemetery.
Fort Kochi on foot or by bicycle.
Puducherry's French Quarter in the early morning.

safety: Timings, closures and tickets change; check official sources before you go.
Churches in Goa and Kochi are places of worship; dress modestly and avoid visiting during services.
Many heritage buildings are working offices; photograph from public spaces only.

faqs.q: Which colonial buildings in India are UNESCO sites?
faqs.a: The Churches and Convents of Goa, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, and Mumbai's Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles.

faqs.q: Where is the French Quarter in India?
faqs.a: In Puducherry, on the coast of Tamil Nadu.

faqs.q: Which city has the most British-era architecture?
faqs.a: Kolkata and Mumbai have the richest ensembles.

faqs.q: When did Portuguese rule end in Goa?

faqs.a: A colonial prison in Port Blair where freedom fighters were held, now a national memorial.
